stories.title: Sunbird relaunches its iMessage-for-Android app, three years after privacy scandal shut it down
stories.summary: Sunbird has brought back its app that lets Android users send and receive iMessages, roughly three years after pulling it amid a major privacy backlash. The original launch was scrapped when researchers found the app was mishandling user messages and credentials. The relaunch marks another attempt to solve the long-standing blue-bubble/green-bubble divide between iPhone and Android messaging.
stories.whyItMatters: Cross-platform iMessage access remains a recurring flashpoint in the mobile industry, and any credible attempt touches Apple's messaging lock-in and the security scrutiny that follows unofficial iMessage bridges.
whatToWatch: Whether security researchers re-examine the relaunched app for the same class of privacy issues
How Apple responds, if at all, to a renewed unofficial iMessage client
questions: What specifically was fixed from the original privacy failure?
Is the new version built on different technical infrastructure than the 2023 app?

stories.title: SpaceX's debut public earnings report unsettles investors
stories.summary: SpaceX released its first public earnings statement, and the numbers reportedly spooked investors, according to Ars Technica. Engadget frames the disclosure as showing a financial profile more typical of an AI company than a traditional space and satellite launch business.
stories.whyItMatters: SpaceX is one of the most valuable private companies in tech, and any hint of financial strain or unusual spending patterns has ripple effects across the launch, satellite-internet, and AI infrastructure markets it touches.
whatToWatch: Further detail on what specifically alarmed investors in the report

stories.title: MacPaw partners with Liquid AI to bring on-device inference to its app store developers
stories.summary: MacPaw, the maker of CleanMyMac and operator of its own app store, is teaming up with Liquid AI to give developers building for that store access to on-device AI inference. TechCrunch reports the move as an effort to make local, on-device AI models easier to integrate into third-party apps.
stories.whyItMatters: On-device inference partnerships reflect a broader industry push to run AI locally rather than in the cloud, which affects cost, privacy, and latency for app developers.

stories.title: Apple's Private Relay can leak your real IP address, TechCrunch warns
stories.summary: TechCrunch published a PSA-style report warning that Apple's Private Relay privacy feature can, under certain conditions, leak a user's real IP address rather than masking it as intended.
stories.whyItMatters: Private Relay is one of Apple's flagship privacy features across iOS and macOS, so any leak undermines a core promise Apple makes to hundreds of millions of users about browsing anonymity.

stories.title: Disney+ partners with TikTok to bring fan-made shorts to its short-form video feed
stories.summary: Disney is partnering with TikTok to surface fan-created short-form video content within Disney+, according to Engadget and TechCrunch. The move brings creator content from TikTok into Disney's own streaming app rather than keeping it siloed on TikTok.

stories.title: Analysis: SpaceX's business looks more like X than Space these days
stories.summary: Following SpaceX's debut public earnings disclosure, The Verge argues the company's financial picture is increasingly shaped by its ties to X (formerly Twitter) rather than its rocket and satellite operations.
